function.mechanism: Scavenges lipid radicals and interrupts oxidation chain reactions in fats and oils.
common_food_categories: Processed foods using tocopherols as antioxidants

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation (E306-E309) reported it could not establish an ADI due limited toxicity data, while concluding no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses/use levels; data insufficient to derive a numerical ADI.

fda.notes: Tocopherols are GRAS under GMP (182.3890). Alpha-tocopherols in 184.1890 are affirmed as GRAS with use limited to nitrosamine inhibition in pump-cured bacon at GMP while broader evaluation continues.

adi.basis: Group ADI range 0.15-2 mg/kg bw/day for dl-alpha-tocopherol and d-alpha-tocopherol concentrate; value field stores upper bound.

concerns.summary: JECFA human studies reported increased bleeding time at >2 mg/kg bw/day and slight increases at 1-2 mg/kg bw/day; a 2025 PubMed case report described reversible coagulopathy after vitamin E excess.
A 2024 meta-analysis found no stroke prevention benefit from vitamin E alone and reported increased hemorrhagic stroke risk when vitamin E was combined with other antioxidants (RR 1.22).

The SELECT trial (2011) found increased prostate cancer risk with 400 IU/day all-rac-alpha-tocopheryl acetate supplementation (HR 1.17); this reflects supplement-dose exposure rather than typical additive intake.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2015) reported no safety concern at reported food-additive uses/use levels for E306-E309.
FDA/eCFR retains GRAS status for tocopherols in Title 21.
No IARC monograph classification was identified for alpha-tocopherol.

populations: Children with high intake relative to body weight
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA did not set a numerical ADI and reported one children survey exceeding UL; JECFA provides a finite ADI range (0.15-2 mg/kg bw/day).

risk_assessment.rationale: E307 remains approved/GRAS, but EFSA could not establish an ADI, EFSA identified a child UL exceedance signal in one survey, and JECFA/PubMed data support coagulation-related concern at higher exposures. Evidence for harm at ordinary additive exposure remains limited, so overall risk is best characterized as moderate rather than high.
key_factors: EFSA 2015 no-safety-concern conclusion at reported uses but no ADI established
FDA GRAS status with specific CFR use conditions
JECFA ADI range 0.15-2 mg/kg bw/day and human bleeding-time findings
Recent PubMed high-dose safety signals (coagulopathy, hemorrhagic stroke context)
No IARC classification and no major-jurisdiction bans identified
